compound_ladder.label: calibrated (0.21% of lap time)
compound_ladder.derivation: fresh-tyre step prior 0.164 s (calibrated (0.21% of lap time)). The races identify the *net* cost of one step harder over a whole stint, holding stint length and race phase fixed: Barcelona 2023 -0.042 +/- 0.131 s; Barcelona 2025 +0.343 +/- 0.489 s [not used: standard error 0.489 s > 0.15 s (pre-2026 measurement, too imprecise to pool)]; australia-2026 +0.317 +/- 0.345 s; japan-2026 -0.069 +/- 0.664 s; austria-2026 +0.106 +/- 0.295 s; belgium-2026 +0.075 +/- 0.323 s; hungary-2026 -0.010 +/- 0.327 s; italy-2026 +0.173 +/- 0.354 s -> pooled +0.058 +/- 0.113 s per step. The model's fresh-tyre offsets are calibrated so that, with its own degradation ladder, it reproduces this net at the stint length it recommends.

pace_offset_s.note: the level of the car's clean long-run laps against the field's own compound/age trend; negative is quicker than the field.  It is confounded by the run programme - practice long runs differ in fuel load and in how hard they are being driven, and neither is observable here - so it is reported, not charged: no cost in the objective reads it (see car_terms)

deg_rate_by_compound.note: the field rate plus the fit's own dev[d, c], pooled driver -> team by percar.team_pooled_dev at k = 20 clean laps; the team -> field step is the fit's own hierarchical pull on dev (sigma_dev ~ HalfNormal(0.02)) and is not applied twice here

age_sensitivity.note: the same pooled deviation as one number: how much more lap time per lap of tyre age this car gives away than the field

warmup_s.note: mean excess of laps 1/2 of a stint over that stint's own trend (fitted from lap 3); in a practice table lap 1 is the out-lap and is filtered out, so this is normally the first flying lap.  A pool of fewer than 2 stints contributes nothing

consistency_s.note: residual SD about the stint trend, over the laps the trend was fitted on

traffic_sensitivity.note: the car's excess over the stint trend within 2 s of the car ahead, divided by the field's same excess (0.715 s/lap over 45 laps); 1.0 is a car that loses what everyone loses

push_response.note: not identifiable pre-race: a practice long run is a full-push experiment by construction, so this weekend carries no within-car variation in push from which a per-car management response could be estimated.  The calibrated team/field value is used, fully shrunk

sector_deg.note: per-sector slope against tyre age over this car's long runs, from the FastF1 cache's sector times

pace_vs_teammate_s.note: this car's level minus BOR's, shrunk toward 0 (the two cars are the same car) by the thinner of the two samples

terms.note: warmup_s and traffic_mult are field-relative: a car with no evidence gets the calibrated field values unchanged

explanation: OCO: 2-stop M-H-M @ 18,40; BEA: 3-stop M-S-H-S @ 12,28,48 - first stops differ by 6 laps (OCO lap 18, BEA lap 12); different shapes (MEDIUM-HARD-MEDIUM vs MEDIUM-SOFT-HARD-SOFT)

pace level: OCO 0.886 s/lap vs BEA 0.434 s/lap (+0.453); the quicker car reaches any given gap to the car ahead sooner, which moves the lap its stop is worth taking [OCO: n=9, w=0.53, driver | BEA: n=13, w=0.62, driver]
S3 degradation: OCO +0.0019 vs BEA +0.0409 s/lap of age (-0.0390); it says *where* the loss is, and enters no cost [OCO: n=12, w=0.50, driver | BEA: n=10, w=0.45, team]

consistency: OCO 0.99 s vs BEA 0.55 s (+0.437); a wider spread about the stint trend is uncertainty, not a cost: it widens the window rather than moving the lap [OCO: n=8, w=0.40, team | BEA: n=9, w=0.43, team]

race-history rate factor (from previous races, not this weekend's evidence): OCO x1.011 vs BEA x1.214 after precision shrinkage (raw x1.022 / x1.389, ln_sd 0.09699590292292087 / 0.08337136379678502); it scales the whole rate, so the higher factor stops earlier
S1 degradation: OCO +0.0248 vs BEA +0.0073 s/lap of age (+0.0175); it says *where* the loss is, and enters no cost [OCO: n=12, w=0.50, driver | BEA: n=10, w=0.45, team]

degradation on MEDIUM: OCO 0.2291 vs BEA 0.2426 s/lap of age (-0.0135); BEA pays 0.3 s more than OCO over a 25-lap stint, which pulls its stop earlier [OCO: n=9, w=0.31, team | BEA: n=13, w=0.39, team]
S2 degradation: OCO +0.0712 vs BEA +0.0651 s/lap of age (+0.0062); it says *where* the loss is, and enters no cost [OCO: n=12, w=0.50, driver | BEA: n=10, w=0.45, team]

traffic sensitivity: OCO 1.27x vs BEA 1.12x (+0.156); the more traffic-sensitive car pays more for rejoining into the pack, which pushes its stop toward a clearer lap [OCO: n=3, w=0.33, team | BEA: n=0, w=0.00, team]
